title: RFC 3986 URI Normalization Test Corpus
profile: Absolute HTTP/HTTPS URIs. RFC 3986 sections 6.2.2.1, 6.2.2.2, 6.2.2.3, and 6.2.3 (with RFC 5.2.4 dot-segment removal and BDEW API-Webdienste 1.2 section 3.3 query preservation).
assumptions: Inputs are ASCII URI strings targeting absolute http or https resources (relative references without scheme, and non-http/https schemes, are rejected in the strict HTTP/HTTPS profile; generic RFC 3986 variants are tested separately in profile_dependent_tests).

Strict RFC 3986 parsing applies: empty hosts (e.g. 'http://', 'http:///a', 'http://:80/a') and missing '//' authority delimiters (e.g. 'http:/a') are rejected per RFC 9110 sections 4.2.1/4.2.2 and RFC 3986 section 6.2.3.
Percent-encoding decoding applies strictly in a single pass to RFC 3986 section 2.3 unreserved ASCII octets only (ALPHA / DIGIT / '-' / '.' / '_' / '~'); '%25' is never double-decoded.
Consecutive slashes ('//') and trailing slashes ('/a/') are preserved byte-for-byte; RFC 3986 does not collapse empty path segments.
Query parameters are preserved in exact order with duplicates, empty values, valueless keys, '+' literals, and empty '?' delimiters intact (BDEW 3.3 and RFC 3986 6.2.3).

IPv6 address literals undergo hex lowercasing per RFC 3986 section 3.2.2 without mandatory RFC 5952 zero-compression; trailing DNS dots are preserved per RFC 3986 (see profile_dependent_tests for stricter/extended variants).
Idempotence invariant: for every valid test case, normalize(expected) MUST equal expected.
recommended_order: 1. Validate raw input against strict RFC 3986 URI syntax and HTTP/HTTPS profile requirements (reject empty/whitespace/non-ASCII/invalid percent-escapes/missing scheme/missing '//' authority/empty host).
2. Parse into components: (scheme, authority[userinfo, host, port], path, query, fragment) before modifying any component.

3. Syntax-Based Normalization (6.2.2.1 & 6.2.2.2) per component: lowercase scheme; normalize host (lowercase IP-literal hex; for reg-name decode unreserved %XX, lowercase ASCII letters including decoded ones, uppercase hex digits of remaining %XX); for path and query (and userinfo/fragment if accepted), perform single-pass decoding of unreserved %XX (preserving letter case) and uppercase hex digits of all remaining %XX triplets.

4. Path Segment Normalization (6.2.2.3): apply RFC 3986 section 5.2.4 remove_dot_segments exclusively to the path component (after percent-encoding normalization so %2e/%2E is handled, while %2f/%2F remains a segment byte, and never touching query or fragment).

5. Scheme-Based Normalization (6.2.3 / RFC 9110 4.2.3): remove explicit ':' and port if port is empty or numerically equal to the scheme default (80 for http, 443 for https, including zero-padded forms such as :080 or :00443); normalize empty path to '/'. Preserve empty '?' delimiter.
6. Recompose the normalized URI per RFC 3986 section 5.3.

Path, query, and decoded unreserved characters outside host remain case-sensitive.

sections.description: RFC 3986 6.2.2.2: decode percent-encoded octets for ASCII unreserved characters (ALPHA / DIGIT / '-' / '.' / '_' / '~') in a single pass. Keep encoded reserved, non-ASCII, and '%' octets encoded with uppercase hex digits. Never alter valid unencoded reserved characters or convert '+' to/from space.

profile_dependent_tests.policy_question: Does the normalizer target RFC 3986 section 4.3 absolute-URI / RFC 9110 http-URI (fragments forbidden) or RFC 3986 section 3 URI (fragments allowed and empty '#' preserved)?
profile_dependent_tests.purpose: RFC 3986 6.2.3 explicitly forbids stripping trailing '#' when fragments are supported.
When fragments are supported, empty path still becomes '/' before '#frag'.
When fragments are supported, percent-encoding normalization applies, case is preserved, and remove_dot_segments does NOT run on fragment.

profile_dependent_tests.policy_question: Does the HTTP/HTTPS profile reject deprecated userinfo per RFC 9110 section 4.2.4, or normalize it per RFC 3986 6.2.2?
profile_dependent_tests.purpose: RFC 3986 userinfo preserves case and normalizes percent-encodings.

profile_dependent_tests.policy_question: Userinfo rejected per RFC 9110 4.2.4 vs preserved per RFC 3986 6.2.3.
profile_dependent_tests.purpose: RFC 3986 6.2.3 states empty delimiters in userinfo must not be stripped.

profile_dependent_tests.policy_question: HTTP/HTTPS-only scheme filter vs generic RFC 3986 URI normalizer.
HTTP/HTTPS-only vs generic syntax-only vs scheme-aware mailto normalization.
profile_dependent_tests.purpose: RFC 3986 section 6.2.3 scheme-specific hostname normalization inside opaque mailto path.

profile_dependent_tests.policy_question: Pure RFC 3986 3.2.2 ABNF first-match fallback to reg-name vs strict IPv4/DNS validation.
profile_dependent_tests.purpose: In RFC 3986 3.2.2 ABNF, non-IPv4 dotted-quad matches reg-name unless DNS/IPv4 semantics reject it.

profile_dependent_tests.policy_question: Pure RFC 3986 reg-name fallback vs WHATWG/strict IPv4 rejection.
profile_dependent_tests.purpose: RFC 3986 dec-octet forbids leading zeros, so 012.0.0.1 parses as reg-name (never octal 10.0.0.1!).

profile_dependent_tests.policy_question: TCP 16-bit port range check (0..65535) vs pure RFC 3986 port = *DIGIT.
profile_dependent_tests.purpose: RFC 3986 section 3.2.3 syntax allows arbitrary *DIGIT without a 65535 cap.

profile_dependent_tests.policy_question: Numeric canonicalization of leading zeros on non-default ports vs literal retention.
profile_dependent_tests.purpose: RFC 3986 6.2.3 only mandates eliding default/empty ports; stripping leading zeros on non-default ports varies by implementation.

profile_dependent_tests.policy_question: Pure RFC 3986 hex lowercasing vs RFC 5952 canonical IPv6 compression.
profile_dependent_tests.purpose: Distinguish RFC 3986 3.2.2 from RFC 5952 IPv6 canonical text representation.
